text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed sharply higher on the back of a speculative New York-led rally. October whites rose by $4.40 to close at $328.60 per tonne. December added $3.80 to close at $325.40 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended sharply higher, with all delivery months up to January 1999 seeing new contract highs. October closed 31 points higher at 11.86 cents/lb, while March added 27 points to close at 12.05 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 21 and 22 points. In spite of current ample supplies funds decided to go long anticipating a tight supply situation in 1997/98. Although first forecasts for the upcoming season point to a limited reduction in stocks, a sharp rise in prices does not seem to be fundamentally justified as stocks are still fairly high. However, there is ongoing concern about how the El Nino weather pattern would affect sugar crops in Thailand, Australia and Asia in general. These fears could keep prices firm in spite of sluggish enduser demand.

NORTHERN GERMANY ** - The second beet test in the Northern German growing area shows that root weight is still high while sugar content was able to pick up given the dry and sunny weather in recent days. Beet weight per ha on August 14 reached 42.8 tonnes, 27.4 per cent up on the previous year's 38.6 tonnes. Sugar content amounted to 14.87 per cent compared to 14.75 per cent in 1996. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 6.36 tonnes, white value, per ha, 12 per cent up on the 5.67 tonnes of 1996. A leaf weight of 631 grams per root (1996 543 grams) and a rather high average number of plants per ha of 85,700 units (86,400) indicates that the crop has still very good potential for improvement.

GERMANY ** - Sugar imports in April 1997 amounted to 12,350 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from 28,734 tonnes in April 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first seven months of 1996/97 (October/April) up to 124,238 tonnes against 130,259 tonnes in 1995/96. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 206,911 tonnes against 225,848 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were France with 86,669 tonnes whites against 96,727 tonnes and the Netherlands with 14,129 tonnes against 9,024 tonnes.

Sugar exports in April 1997 reached 121,911 tonnes against 86,880 tonnes in April 1996. This brought cumulative exports in October/April 1996/97 up to 1.005 million tonnes against 964,668 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 1.316 million tonnes, down from 1.452 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Italy with 129,680 tonnes whites against 50,563 tonnes, Belgium-Luxembourg with 126,064 tonnes, up from 106,655 tonnes, the United Arab Emirates with 113,606 tonnes compared to 111,453 tonnes and Switzerland with 57,884 tonnes, down from 63,615 tonnes.

BRAZIL ** - Sugar production in June 1997 amounted to 1.207 million tonnes which compares to 1.500 million tonnes in June 1996. This brought cumulative production in the first two months of 1997/98 (May/June) up to 2.724 million tonnes against 1.957 million tonnes in 1996/97. Total production in 1996/97 reached the record high of 14.732 million tonnes against 13.661 million tonnes in 1995/96.

Alcohol production in the first two months of 1997/98 amounted to 3.464 bln litres against 3.060 bln litres in the corresponding period the previous year. The production of hydrous alcohol is still racing ahead accounting for 71.2 per cent of the total while anhydrous alcohol accounted for the balance.
